title: Boundary vanishing for an open-supported proper direct image over a qcqs base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring $\Lambda$ of [sk-def-localizing-closure]: a finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, where $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite inside a fixed algebraic closure, with exactly the condensed-ring convention of that node. For a scheme $T$ put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$, the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme, let $q:Z\to S$ and $q':Z'\to S$ be proper morphisms, and let $h:Z'\to Z$ be a proper morphism with $qh=q'$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ and $j':U\hookrightarrow Z'$ be quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] satisfying $hj'=j$ and $h^{-1}(j(U))=j'(U)$ as open subschemes. Let $i:B\hookrightarrow Z$ be any closed immersion with underlying image $Z\setminus j(U)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every
$$K\in\operatorname{Loc}(\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(U,\Lambda)),$$
where $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}$ is the bounded constructible finite-Tor-amplitude subcategory and $\operatorname{Loc}$ is its ambient replete triangulated closure under small direct sums [sk-def-localizing-closure], one has
$$i^*Rh_*D(j'_!)K\simeq0\quad\text{in }D_B.$$
Here $D(j'_!)$ is exact termwise module extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and $i^*$ is the exact inverse image with the pulled-back coefficient ring. Neither density of $U$ in $Z$ or $Z'$, nor a field, characteristic, Noetherian or finite-dimensional-base assumption is imposed.

proof.text: All inverse images here are the actual module-object pullbacks. By [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] their coefficient-change maps are isomorphisms. Thus the formula for pullback in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] identifies the underlying abelian sheaf with ordinary inverse image. That inverse image is exact by [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image](4), and [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-lifted] makes the module lift exact. These statements hold for every commutative condensed ring, so apply also to the precise algebraic-closure coefficient specified here. The exact functors act termwise on derived categories by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization].

source.place: Coefficient typing before the closed-complement calculation.

proof.text: Form $B'=Z'\times_ZB$, with projections $a:B'\hookrightarrow Z'$ and $h_B:B'\to B$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The base-change assertions of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b) make $a$ a closed immersion and $h_B$ proper. The image of $a$ is $h^{-1}(|B|)$: on an affine chart the pullback of a closed subscheme defined by an ideal $I$ is defined by its extended ideal, whose vanishing set is the inverse image of $V(I)$. Thus its complementary open is $h^{-1}(j(U))=j'(U)$ by hypothesis. This proves that $a$ and $j'$ have complementary images even when $B'$ is nonreduced. The complementary open immersions $j,j'$ are quasi-compact by hypothesis. The two general proper inputs below are formulated with the given proper $q:Z\to S$ over the qcqs scheme $S$, so no unstated finite-type-over-a-field or global-dimension inference is needed.

Put $J=D(j'_!)$. It carries $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(U,\Lambda)$ into $\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Z',\Lambda)$. To check this, use exactness of $j'_!$ from [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]: $H^n(JK)=j'_!H^n(K)$, with the same bounds. Check constructibility on each affine open $V$ of $Z'$. Its inverse-image open $U_V$ is quasi-compact by quasi-compactness of $j'$, hence qcqs as an open of an affine. The restriction of each constructible cohomology sheaf has a finite stratification on $U_V$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. View those strata in $V$ and add $V\setminus U_V$, with zero local model. The source local models are unchanged on the old strata. These strata are constructible in $V$: quasi-compact opens in the quasi-separated spaces $U_V,V$ are retrocompact, so each Boolean expression in those opens on $U_V$ remains one on $V$, intersected with $U_V$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Local closedness is retained under an open inclusion. Extension by zero is computed on these localized opens by the same defining extension/sheafification. On the old strata $j'_!H^n(K)$ restricts to $H^n(K)$, because the open unit $j'^*j'_!\to\mathrm{id}$ is invertible, and on $V\setminus U_V$ its restriction is zero by the mixed restriction $i^*j_!=0$ for a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement; both are assertions of [lem-sfb-condensed-support-derived-localization]. This checks constructibility of $j'_!H^n(K)$ locally on every affine $V$, which is the condition of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] on an arbitrary scheme. When $Z'$ is qcqs, choose a finite affine cover $V_1,\dots,V_m$ and stratify $Z'$ by the sets $T\cap(V_k\setminus(V_1\cup\dots\cup V_{k-1}))$, $T$ a stratum chosen on $V_k$: each $V_k$ is a retrocompact open of the quasi-separated $Z'$, so these finitely many pairwise disjoint sets are constructible and locally closed in $Z'$ [def-weil-constructible-subset], they cover $Z'$, and on each the restriction keeps the finite constant local model of $T$. This gives the global stratification of the qcqs clause. Finally, for a sheaf $N$ on $Z'$ the general open projection formula [lem-sfb-condensed-support-projection-formula] gives $JK\otimes^{\mathbf L}N\simeq J(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}j'^*N)$. The pullback is exact by step 1 and $J$ is exact, so every finite Tor interval for $K$ remains a Tor interval for $JK$. This proves the assertion directly from the definition; no Noetherian extension lemma is used.

proof.text: For a generator $K\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(U,\Lambda)$ apply [lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-constructible-closed-base-change] with $f=h$, $c=i$ and $L=JK$. The scheme $S$ is qcqs and $q:Z\to S$ and $h$ are proper by hypothesis, the open complement of $i$ is the given quasi-compact $j$, and step 3 gives the required finite-Tor constructibility. It follows that $i^*Rh_*JK\simeq R(h_B)_*a^*JK$. The mixed-restriction assertion of [lem-sfb-condensed-support-derived-localization], applied to $a$ and $j'$, gives $a^*JK\simeq0$. A right adjoint preserves the zero object: by the adjunction in [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], maps from any object into $R(h_B)_*0$ are in bijection with maps into $0$, hence form a singleton. Therefore $i^*Rh_*JK\simeq0$ on every generator.

source.place: (2) Isomorphism: closed-complement vanishing for the bounded generators.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], $J$ and $i^*$ are triangulated. Their sheaf adjunctions, from [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], induce derived adjunctions, for $J$ by [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]; hence both preserve small ambient coproducts by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. The inverse image under $J$ of $\operatorname{Loc}(\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(Z',\Lambda))$ is therefore a replete triangulated subcategory closed under small sums and contains all source generators by step 3. The minimality in [sk-def-localizing-closure] shows that $J$ sends the source localizing hull into that target hull. Now [lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-localizing-coproducts], applied with the given qcqs $S$ and proper $q:Z\to S$ and $h$, makes $Rh_*J$ preserve small sums on the source hull. The composite $F=i^*Rh_*J$ also preserves these sums. It is triangulated because $Rh_*$ is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], and the other two factors are triangulated as just checked.

source.place: (2) Isomorphism, first paragraph: extension from generators uses ambient coproduct preservation.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Loc}(\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(U,\Lambda))$ consisting of $K$ with $F(K)\simeq0$. It is replete. Since $F$ is triangulated, its kernel is closed under shifts and distinguished triangles: in the image triangle, if two objects are zero, exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(T,-)$ for all $T$ forces the third to be zero. Since $F$ preserves small sums, a sum of objects of $\mathcal C$ maps to a sum of zero objects, again zero, including the empty sum. Thus $\mathcal C$, viewed in $D_U$, is a full replete triangulated subcategory closed under the ambient small sums. Step 4 places every generator in $\mathcal C$. The defining minimality of [sk-def-localizing-closure] now gives $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Loc}(\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(U,\Lambda))$. This is exactly $i^*Rh_*D(j'_!)K\simeq0$ for every $K$ in the stated domain.
